description: Candidate example cars and their estimated value when new (v0). The page picks, for each slot, the youngest model year whose estimated value fits the user's maximum price: value(age) = v0 x the page's depreciation curve (AGE_DEP).

source.name: Verohallinto / Finnish Tax Administration: applied taxation values of passenger cars, 2025 and 2026 (January-September)

method: v0 = median over the model's tax decisions (filter 'vero') of taxation value / depreciation(age), age = decision date - first registration, depreciation = the page's AGE_DEP curve; rounded to 100. Computed by tools/budget_values.py. Model years available come from the Traficom register (catalogue field 'years', 5th-95th percentile of first registration); a discontinued model's last model year caps the range (e-Golf 2020, Auris 2019), because the register's 95th percentile also includes later imports.

rules.petrol: Volkswagen Golf: the petrol Golf (model years up to 2020) or, when the budget fits a younger car, the Golf eTSI mild hybrid (2020-); the youngest that fits, the petrol Golf on a tie.
rules.hybrid: Toyota Corolla if it fits the budget, else Auris, else Yaris (the most common full hybrids).
rules.electric: Of the candidates that fit the budget, the one with the most cars in the Finnish register. If none fits, the cheapest one, flagged as over budget.

list_prices: list_price = importer's price for the cheapest version incl. car tax and VAT, without dealer delivery costs or options, checked 2026-11-17. For comparison only; the page uses v0 from the Tax Administration's values, which describe the cars actually imported (usually better equipped). Golf and Niro agree within 1-2%; Corolla and Yaris v0 are near the dearest trim; Tesla and Kona list prices are for newer cheaper versions or a new generation.
